finding.text: `grip.css:270-276` (diff) deletes the `html.grip-sizing { --rail-ease: 0s; cursor: ew-resize; user-select: none; }` rule (and its comment) while adding the new `.grip-y` block in its place — the rule is never re-added anywhere else in the patch. That rule is what kills the shell's drag-easing lag, forces the resize cursor, and stops text selection during every drag, on the x-axis too. Losing it breaks deliverable 1's "byte-identical" promise for every existing caller (drawer, DevBar, Sidebar, Shell) — dragging any rail will now feel laggy (0.18s trail) and can select page text mid-drag. Grep confirms `--rail-ease` only appears once in the whole diff, as a deletion (`grep -n "rail-ease" diff.patch` → line 270 only, no `+` line).

`rail.js`'s `size()` writes a saved localStorage height straight to `--sheet-h` with no clamp against the current viewport, unlike `handle()`'s `write` callback which clamps to `window.innerHeight * 0.92`. A height saved on a tall viewport (tablet landscape) and reopened on a short one (phone portrait) could set a `max-block-size` taller than the screen; since the sheet is `position: fixed; inset-block-end: 0`, a genuinely tall thread could push the sheet's top off-screen with no way to reach it. Worth a one-line `Math.min(saved, window.innerHeight * 0.92)` guard to match `write`'s own ceiling.

`doc/decisions.md`'s own verification write-up says the touch proof measured a strip at "20px" for the 1.25rem coarse-pointer width, but `grip.css`'s touch block sets `width: 1.25rem` = 20px only at the browser default 16px root font-size — true in the test, but worth flagging since the file's own `rem` warning earlier ("the dev rail's text is 0.8rem…") shows root size assumptions have bitten this module before; no evidence here that it's wrong, just that the number is viewport/zoom-dependent and not restated as such.

answer.reply: fixed: restored html.grip-sizing { --rail-ease: 0s; user-select: none } unconditionally, plus made the cursor axis-aware (grip.js now stamps grip-sizing-x/grip-sizing-y alongside grip-sizing; grip.css gives each its own cursor: ew-resize / ns-resize). Verified during a real drag on both axes with an actual Playwright pointer session (a bare dispatchEvent can't establish an active pointer for setPointerCapture, which silently threw and made an earlier check look broken until this was accounted for).

fixed: pulled the clamp into one clamp_height(px) method (Math.min(Math.max(px,160), innerHeight*0.92)) that both handle()'s write() and size()'s saved-height path now call, so a height read back from localStorage is clamped exactly like a live drag is.

fixed: added a clause to decisions.md noting the 12px/20px strip measurements are at the browser's default 16px root font size, next to this file's own existing rem-not-em rule which already leans on the same assumption.
